prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. Injury: shoulder injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1230; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this case. Is that acceptable?

Q: I'm going to need your name for the transcript, sir. Let's keep it simple.

A: Fine. [Plaintiff name].

Q: Thank you. Now, can you describe the collision that occurred in Baytown, Texas?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road heading toward the shopping center. Traffic was light. A car crossed into my lane and we hit nose to nose. It wasn't a violent crash, but it happened fast enough that my airbags went off.

Q: What was your speed at the moment of impact, to the best of your recollection?

A: I wasn't going fast. I'd guess I was doing maybe twenty-five miles an hour, and I had already started slowing when I saw the other car coming toward me.

Q: Did you have any injuries immediately after the collision?

A: My neck felt stiff, and my right shoulder hurt right away. I didn't think much of it at first. I figured it would work itself out.

Q: When did you first seek medical treatment?

A: I went to the emergency room later that same day because the shoulder pain got worse overnight. They took X-rays and told me nothing was broken, but I had a serious strain.

Q: Since then, what treatment have you received for the shoulder?

A: I've been going to physical therapy about twice a week. My doctor gave me exercises to do at home, and I've had a couple of injections to help with the pain. Some days it's better, some days I can barely lift a gallon of milk.

Q: Has your shoulder limited your daily activities?

A: Yes, a lot. I used to coach my son's soccer team and I've had to step back from that. Simple things like reaching into the cupboard or putting on a jacket are harder. I've also had trouble sleeping because I can't find a comfortable position.

Q: Have you missed any work because of your injury?

A: I've missed some days, mostly for appointments, and I've had to switch to lighter duties at work for a while. My supervisor has been accommodating, but it's not the same job I was doing before.

Q: Before this accident, did you have any prior injuries or problems with that same shoulder?

A: No. I played college baseball years ago, but I never had any shoulder trouble that required a doctor. I've been pretty healthy overall.

Q: Do you currently expect any further treatment?

A: My doctor mentioned that I might need more therapy, and possibly a follow-up scan if the pain doesn't improve. I'm hoping it gets better on its own, but I honestly don't know yet.
